volume.action: REUSED AND MOVED, NOT CREATED. The project was at Railway's hard 20-volume cap, so create-volume was refused.
volume.why_this_volume: its name records that it WAS l5-pmus-live's own state volume. Moving it back is non-destructive and keeps whatever history it holds, where deleting any volume to free a cap slot would have destroyed data the owner did not authorize losing.
volume.data_destroyed: NONE. update-volume moves a volume and keeps its contents.

variable.name: L5_LIVE_ROOT
variable.why_deviated: the moved volume may still contain an l5-live/ directory from when it was this service's volume. Mounting at /data and pointing the root at /data/l5-live could have RELOADED stale state and resurrected the very phantom being cleared, which is the opposite of reconstructing from venue evidence. A dated root is unambiguously fresh and leaves any old data intact beside it for forensics.
variable.applied_with: skipDeploys, so the volume attach carried both into ONE deployment as instructed
